reconcile.connective: Defenders dissolve the conflict by denying the premise: the Genesis 6 "sons of God" are the godly Sethite line, not angels, since Christ says angels cannot marry.

discrepancy.connective: Hermann Gunkel, reading Genesis 6 on its own terms, insists the "sons of God" are divine beings whose union with women produced the Nephilim — precisely the angelic procreation Mark 12:25 forecloses.

excerpts.excerpt_text: This is quite sufficient of itself to exclude any reference to angels. For Christ Himself distinctly states that the angels cannot marry (Mat 22:30; Mar 12:25; cf. Luk 20:34.).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: K&D explicitly use Mark 12:25 (angels cannot marry) to rule out the angelic reading of the Genesis 6 'sons of God', directly addressing the alleged contradiction by denying angels ever had sex.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Genesis 6:1-4
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D's note on Genesis 6 mounts an extended harmonizing defense of the Sethite reading, arguing from Mark 12:25 that the 'sons of God' cannot be angels and that Jude 6-7 does not describe angel marriages.
